sections.h2: How do you sell a house in State College, PA?
sections.html:
Three routes exist: a listing, a private sale, or a straight sale to a buyer who accepts the place in its present state. Each one finishes with a deed recorded in Centre County and the transfer tax paid. What varies is the prep work and the calendar.

State College is a home rule municipality of 4.56 square miles, and it became a borough on August 29, 1896. The Penn State campus known as University Park sits partly inside the borough and partly in neighboring College Township, and that campus shapes who owns, rents and buys here more than anything else.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about housing in State College?
sections.html:
Census estimates put the 2025 population at 40,844. The 2020 count was 40,501 and the 2010 count was 42,034, so headcount has been nearly flat for fifteen years. Those residents share 4.56 square miles, roughly 8,890 per square mile.

Owners live in only 26.1 percent of the homes, and the middle owned home was valued at $437,800 in the 2020 to 2024 survey period. Gross rent runs $1,273 a month and household income $45,424. A household averages 2.24 people, and under 6 percent of residents are children.

So much of the housing here is rented that buyers often ask first whether a house carries a rental permit or a student home license. Have those papers ready.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax applies to a sale inside State College Borough?
sections.html:
Three percent of the price, against 2 percent in most Centre County municipalities. The county's rate table shows the borough with a 1.5 percent local share on top of the state and school district shares.

No deed gets recorded until the tax is paid. Sales agreements commonly split it evenly, yet the new owner answers for it if the amount paid is ever questioned. At the median value an even split costs each side $6,567.

Family transfers can be exempt, and so can a deed between ex-spouses. A deed reciting token consideration, say $1, travels with a state Statement of Value for Department of Revenue review.

sections.h2: Do rental permits and student home licenses change how a State College sale works?
sections.html:
They can, because they decide what a buyer may do with the property after closing. The borough hands rental permit administration to Centre Region Code Administration, a body that also covers Patton, Ferguson, College, Half Moon and Harris townships and Bellefonte Borough.

  • Rental Housing Permit: required for any unit lived in by someone other than the owner or the owner's immediate family. The unit must meet the International Property Maintenance Code and the Fire Prevention Code, and an imminent hazard can lead to a vacate order within 10 days and a suspended permit if it is not fixed within 90 days.
  • Student Home License: applies to one-family homes, one-family homes with an accessory apartment, and two-family dwellings occupied by more than one unrelated student. The borough adopted Ordinance 2029 for this in November 2013. An existing license can move to a new owner with an approved transfer application and a $25 fee.
  • New student homes: a first license costs $1,000, with a $50 zoning permit for the change of use and a $25 rental permit application fee. In the R-1, R-2 and R-3 zoning districts a new student home also has to meet spacing rules from existing ones, which is why an already licensed house is worth more to an investor.
  • Short-term rentals: the borough license costs $450 and lasts one year. It requires a rental housing permit, proof the applicant lives there at least eight months a year, off-street parking matching the bedrooms rented, and at least $100,000 of liability insurance.

Student home licenses renew every year, and the 2026 renewal deadline was October 15. Write to studenthomes@statecollegepa.us to confirm a license is current before you tell a buyer it transfers.

sections.h2: How does the valley setting affect a State College house?
sections.html:
At about 1,154 feet in a mountain-ringed valley, the borough feels its weather in basements, roofs and heating bills. January averages 27.2 degrees and July 72.2, a humid continental pattern. Yearly precipitation is 41.53 inches, snowfall 43.8 inches, and snow usually falls between October and April.

The valley floor is prone to frequent rain, snow and flooding. Inspectors here tend to check sump pumps, foundation moisture, gutters and furnace age, so hand over any repair or roof records early.

sections.h2: What will buyers ask about schools, getting around and utilities?
sections.html:
Schools come first. The State College Area School District runs eight elementary schools, two middle schools and one high school for 6,712 students. Three elementary schools sit inside the borough: Coral Street, Radio Park and Easterly Parkway. Mount Nittany Middle School serves most of the borough except College Heights, and the whole district feeds State College Area High School.

  • Roads and transit: U.S. Route 322 Business and Pennsylvania Route 26 run through the borough. The Centre Area Transportation Authority operates buses to College, Ferguson and Patton townships, and State College Regional Airport has daily flights to Charlotte, Chicago, Philadelphia and Washington.
  • Commute: workers average a 15.5 minute trip to the job, the shortest of the four Pennsylvania places the Census compares here.
  • Utilities: West Penn Power supplies electricity, Columbia Gas of Pennsylvania supplies natural gas, the State College Borough Water Authority provides water, the University Area Joint Authority handles sewer, and borough public works collects trash and recycling.
  • Employers: a 2016 list put Penn State at 27,029 employees, Mount Nittany Medical Center at 2,365 and the school district at 1,792.

sections.h2: Which routes sell a State College house fastest?
sections.html:
The quickest routes skip showings and repair haggling. A listing reaches the most people but adds inspection requests, financing contingencies and a closing date that has to suit a lender.

An investor planning a rental may close sooner, especially where a rental permit or student home license is already in place. A direct cash purchase drops the financing step and takes the property as is, with an offer that accounts for repairs. Get price, closing date and the 3 percent tax split in writing before you commit.

sections.h2: What should you confirm before accepting an offer?
sections.html:
• Locate your deed. If it is missing, contact the Centre County Recorder of Deeds.
  • Request a payoff figure from your lender to see what remains after the mortgage clears.
  • Settle who pays the 3 percent transfer tax before you sign.
  • Confirm whether the house has a rental housing permit, student home license or short-term rental license, and disclose it.
  • Gather receipts for roof, furnace, drainage and plumbing work.
  • Check that property tax bills are current, since unpaid balances are deducted at closing.

faqs.q: Is State College's transfer tax really 3 percent?
faqs.a: Yes. Centre County's rate table lists State College Borough at 3.00 percent: 1.00 percent state, 1.5 percent local and 0.50 percent school district. Most other municipalities in the county total 2.00 percent. Buyers and sellers often divide it equally, but the contract decides.

faqs.q: Does a student home license go to the buyer?
faqs.a: Yes. The borough allows an existing student home license to transfer to a new owner once a transfer application is approved and a $25 fee is paid. Email studenthomes@statecollegepa.us for the current transfer application before you advertise the license as part of the sale.

faqs.q: Does a rented house need a rental permit to sell?
faqs.a: The permit is a condition of renting, so a rented house should hold a current Rental Housing Permit from Centre Region Code Administration. Selling does not create a separate permit step in the borough pages. Check the permit status first, because a lapsed permit can worry a buyer.

faqs.q: Who handles trash and water in State College?
faqs.a: Borough public works collects trash and recycling, and the State College Borough Water Authority provides water. Sewer service comes from the University Area Joint Authority. Buyers sometimes ask for these names when they set up accounts.

faqs.q: How can I obtain my State College deed?
faqs.a: Contact the Centre County Recorder of Deeds. The recorder holds the recorded deed, and the office will not accept a new deed for recording until the transfer taxes due have been paid.
